newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Jan 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Jan 31.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Friday's The Wall Street Journal:
* Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan called for the creation of an independent commission to set cost-of-living adjustments for taxes and federal benefits such as Social Security.
* A clause in ITT Corp's articles of incorporation allowing it to expand its board could help the company fight the $6.5 billion hostile bid from Hilton Hotels.
* Mercury Finance's controller denied the firm's contentions that he inflated company profits, a day after the company said accounting irregularities will force it to restate its profits.
* The Dow industrials rose 83.12 points to 6,823.86. The Nasdaq composite rose 15.85 to 1,371.02.
* Gold fell to a 40-month low, losing ground to the government's inflation-indexed bonds.
* Market regulators are preparing to approve the New York Stock Exchange's plan to loosen the "circuit-breakers" meant to halt a panic-driven sell-off.
* The U.S. Food and Drug Adminstration approved a new class of diabetes drug by Warner-Lambert called Rezulin.
* Job advertising fell slightly in December, and the value of new construction contracts dropped six percent.
* The threat of a February 15 strike by pilots of AMR Corp's American Airlines has prompted some customers to make reservations on other carriers.
* Many customers of America Online will be ineligible for the refunds the company is promising to pay.

* Motorola won a federal appeals court ruling allowing it and a sports statistics gathering company to transmit scores from National Basketball Association games taken from radio and television broadcasts.
* An HMO trade group released a policy designed to make it easier for patients to file appeals or get coverage for emergency services.
* Crescent Real Estate Equities' plan to buy a group of psychiatric hospitals from Magellan Health Services muddies its strategy.
* Texas Instruments plans to introduce a computer chip that can process 1.6 billion instructions per second.
* The biggest bets at California's Santa Anita racetrack these days aren't being placed on the horses but on the future of the company that operates the track.

The stock of Santa Anita Cos has more than doubled in just over five months and the company is now officially up for sale following two abortive attempts to take it over at a much lower price. -- Heard on the Street.

* Bond prices rose for the third consecutive day on upbeat economic figures and confidence that the Federal Reserave Board will avoid raising interest rates when it meets next week. But many investors are waiting for the release of important economic data before entering the market. -- Credit Markets.
